chapters.title: How Candide was brought up in a fine castle, and how he was driven therefrom.
paragraphs: In the province of Westphalia, in the castle of the most noble baron of Thunder-ten-tronckh, lived a youth, whom nature had endowed with a most sweet disposition. His face was the true index of his mind. He had a good judgment joined to the most unaffected simplicity; and hence, I presume, he had his name of Candide. The old servants of the house suspected him to be the son of the baron's sister, by a good and worthy gentleman of the neighborhood, whom that young lady would never marry, because he could produce no more than threescore and eleven quarterings in his arms; the rest of his genealogical tree had been lost through time. For his castle had not only a gate, but even windows; and his great hall was hung with tapestry. His pack of hounds was composed of all the dogs of his stables; his grooms served him for huntsmen; and the vicar of the village officiated as grand almoner. He was called My Lord by all his people, and they all laughed when he told stories.
